title: Confirming a trip 500s on Postgres (FK order) and timestamps shift by session timezone
description: Prod /intake/confirm raised ForeignKeyViolation days_base_place_id_fkey: without ORM relationships SQLAlchemy inserted days before places. SQLite tests passed because FKs weren't enforced. Also found via local Postgres: aware datetimes written to TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE were converted through session timezone, breaking geocoding retry timing. Fix: flush parents before children in create_trip, confirm_draft, delete_trip; utcnow() returns naive UTC; tests enforce SQLite FKs and can run on Postgres via TEST_DATABASE_URL.
close_reason: Fixed; 36 tests pass on SQLite (FKs on) and Postgres.

title: Vague base places pin to wrong continent; use chosen hotel as a day's location
description: Prod: 'Central France' pinned to Ville de France, Goiânia, Brazil. Cause: locate_city's settlement-anywhere fallback has no proximity check. Knock-on: hotel options for those days were rejected by the 40 km-from-base guard (base in Brazil), so no option pins. Fix: anywhere-fallback only accepted if in trip countries or within ~1500 km of the trip's other located cities; area-in-countries tried before anywhere. Option/chosen places get retried pins (board + worker share one locator). Map uses a chosen hotel's location for a day's pin and the route when available. Migration resets city pins, clears cache, and re-queues unpinned option places.
close_reason: City fallback now requires trip countries or <=1500 km from trip's other pinned cities (cities pinned in trip order); area-in-countries tried before anywhere. Option and chosen places are retried through the shared locator (board background + worker), with a research map_query field and a leading-town settlement fallback for descriptive names (Clermont-Ferrand city centre..., Blois–Chambord loop...). Map uses a chosen pinned hotel as its base place's pin and in the route. Data migration clears cache, resets city pins, re-queues unpinned options. Regression tests for Central France->Brazil and Holly's Clermont stay; 83 tests on SQLite and Postgres.

title: Add plans to a day: find ideas with AI or add manually
description:
Today each day gets one starter activity gap ('What to do in Lisbon on May 2'). Choosing an option answers it, and there's no way to add a second plan, ask for something specific, or type in a plan you already know.

Goal: a day can hold any number of plans, added two ways from the Day tab's 'Plans for the day' section via an 'Add a plan' button.

1. Find ideas (AI): the traveler says what they want ('dinner near our hotel', 'a morning walk', 'something rainy-day friendly') and optionally a time of day. Creates a new day-scoped activity Gap whose prompt is their request, opens the compare drawer, and runs research with that prompt (existing worker, choose/hide/find more/change all apply). Research context should include the day's already-planned items and chosen stay so ideas fit around them.
2. Add it yourself: short form (name, time of day morning/afternoon/evening/any, optional address or link, notes) that creates an Activity directly with created_by = user. Address/link lookup for a map pin within 40 km of the day's city, same guard as research options.

Also:
- Show plans grouped or ordered by time of day (PRD's morning/afternoon/evening slots); allow reordering.
- Edit and remove a plan. Removing an AI-chosen plan offers to reopen its options; removing a manual one just deletes it (or soft-deletes once travelplanner-266 lands).
- The starter 'What to do' gap stays as the empty-day prompt; once a day has any plan, don't count it as missing.
- Tests: multiple plans per day, custom-prompt research context, manual add with and without a pin, removal paths, privacy.
close_reason: Merged PR #2 into master with share link and deployed 2026-09-16. Add a plan (Find ideas request research with day plans + chosen stay context, or Add it yourself with best-effort pin), time-of-day ordering, reorder, edit, remove (reopen vs delete), starter gap only counts while day empty, Add a plan is the single entry point for day plans. Python review found removed requests still ran paid research; fixed with cancel + worker backstop and tests. 101 tests on SQLite and Postgres; migration checked on Postgres.

title: Geocoding pins cities on unrelated POIs (e.g. Paris -> 'Victor Paris' shop in Edinburgh)
description:
Holly's TdF trip (prod trip a9b1bca9-855c-4493-8827-6f046306aa3a) route loops back to Edinburgh on the last day. Cause: backend/app/geocoding.py _queries_for appends the trip's first destination as free text. When that destination is a city, Nominatim matches POIs/streets containing both words. Verified live 2026-09-16:
- 'Paris, Edinburgh' -> Victor Paris, Dundee Street, Edinburgh (wrong city)
- 'London, Edinburgh' -> The Duke of Edinburgh pub, London (right city by luck)
- 'Leeds, Edinburgh' -> Edinburgh Place, Leeds (right city by luck)
- 'Lille, Edinburgh' -> no match, fell back to 'Lille'

Fix plan:
1. Query Nominatim with featureType=settlement (city/town/village only) and drop free-text destination context; optionally pass countrycodes derived from trip destinations.
2. Sanity-check result addresstype/class before accepting.
3. Tests with fake fetcher asserting params, plus a regression case for 'Paris' with an Edinburgh-first trip.
4. Data cleanup (migration or one-off script run on Render): delete geocode_cache rows whose query contains a comma context, reset lat/lng/precision/geocoded_at on city places so the board re-geocodes. Confirm the TdF trip's Paris pin moves to France.
close_reason: Fixed: geocoding no longer appends destinations as free text. Cities are looked up as featureType=settlement limited to the trip's country codes (resolved per destination, e.g. Scotland->gb), then settlement anywhere, then administrative areas within trip countries; only boundary/place results accepted, so shops/buildings/roads never match. Cache keyed by structured params and stores category/country_code. Migration clears old cache and resets city pins so trips re-geocode on next board load. Regression test for Edinburgh->Paris; migration verified on Postgres and SQLite; live Nominatim located Edinburgh, Leeds, London, Lille, Paris correctly and left Douro Valley unpinned.

title: Soft-delete trips with deleted_at (trash with restore)
description:
Today DELETE /trips/{id} hard-deletes the trip and all children (days, places, gaps, candidates, sources, research jobs, members); no undo. Replace with soft delete.

Plan:
- Migration: add trips.deleted_at (nullable naive-UTC timestamp, indexed).
- DELETE /trips/{id} sets deleted_at = utcnow() instead of removing rows (owner-only, as now).
- Every trip read path excludes deleted trips: list_trips, get_member_trip (404 when deleted), board, days, research start, intake confirm results, worker build_context (fail job if trip deleted), geocoding (skip), future share link (deleted trips never public).
- Trash: GET /trips?deleted=true lists the user's deleted trips; POST /trips/{id}/restore clears deleted_at. Web: 'Recently deleted' section on the trip list with Restore; delete confirm copy says it can be restored for N days.
- Purge: after 30 days, a scheduled job (worker loop or Render cron) hard-deletes children-first with per-table flushes (reuse current delete_trip logic).
- Tests on SQLite (FKs on) and Postgres: deleted trips hidden everywhere, restore works, strangers can't restore, purge removes old ones only, queued research on a deleted trip fails cleanly.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17.

title: Saved places: pin spots to the map without assigning a day
description:
A trip-wide bucket of places the traveler wants on the map but hasn't scheduled: coffee shops, parks, bakeries, viewpoints, shops. Like the TDF planner's places.csv layer.

Data model already mostly supports it: Place is trip-scoped with kind (coffee, food, sight, shop, ...) and nullable coordinates, and Gap.day_id is nullable for trip-wide gaps. Likely additions: a Place.saved flag (or status: saved | scheduled), optional note/tags, and which city it's near.

Scope ideas:
- Board: 'Saved places' tab listing them, grouped by city and kind; map layer toggles per kind (the layer toggles deferred from the planning board epic).
- Add a place by name/link (geocoded server-side, or picked from research results), with a note.
- Research: 'Find coffee shops near our Lisbon base' as a trip-wide gap whose accepted options become saved places, not scheduled activities.
- Later: move a saved place onto a day (becomes an Activity), and show nearby saved places on the Day tab.
- Share link shows saved places as an optional map layer.
close_reason: Merged and deployed 2026-09-17.

title: Verify Clerk token azp (authorized party) in API auth
description:
Hardening. backend/app/auth.py decode_clerk_token verifies RS256 signature, expiry, and issuer, but not the azp claim. Clerk recommends checking azp against the app's allowed frontend origins so a token for this Clerk instance obtained via another site is rejected.

Plan: add AUTHORIZED_PARTIES setting (comma-separated, default from CORS_ORIGINS), reject tokens whose azp is present and not in the list with 401. Tests: valid azp passes, foreign azp 401, missing azp behavior decided explicitly. Update Render env when custom domain lands (travelplanner-bgi).
close_reason: API now rejects Clerk tokens whose azp names a site outside AUTHORIZED_PARTIES (defaults to CORS_ORIGINS, so no Render env change), matching Clerk's authorizedParties rule (azp checked when present). Also requires exp, iat, sub claims. 9 new tests sign real RS256 tokens with a local key: our origins pass, foreign azp/wrong issuer/expired/missing sub/wrong key get 401, plus an end-to-end /me check.

title: Save intake chat history
description:
Today the intake conversation lives only in the browser: refreshing /trips/new loses the chat and draft, and after confirm the conversation is gone. Save it.

Scope ideas:
